discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception, design and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, which was confirmed when the ATLAS and CMS collaborations discovered the Higgs boson in 2012. That discovery would have been impossible without the detectors themselves. Peter Jenni, founding spokesperson of ATLAS, and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee, who conceived CMS and led its design, defined the detector concepts in the late 1980s and early 1990s. These included precision electromagnetic calorimetry for the diphoton channel, powerful muon systems for four-lepton final states, and the radiation-hard technology and trigger architecture needed at unprecedented luminosity. Their vision turned a theoretical necessity into a measured particle. Its mass of about 125 GeV now shows that our vacuum lies near the boundary of electroweak stability, a profound clue about physics beyond the Standard Model. Few experimental achievements have reshaped the questions of fundamental physics so decisively.
